a: “which” önceki yan cümlenin tamamına (yağmur suyunun tutulması) gönderme yapar; bu yüzden geniş zamanda tekil yüklem “reduces” gelir. “reduce” çoğul ister, “reducing” yüklem olamaz, “reduction” isimdir.

s:
Read the paragraph and complete the missing word.

Our town library has started lending more than just books. Residents can now borrow board games, musical instruments and even tools. Librarians say the most popular collection is the gardening equip___, which includes shovels, rakes and hedge trimmers.

Which word correctly completes the unfinished word in the paragraph?
a: “the gardening …” kalıbında belirleyici ve niteleyiciden sonra isim gerekir: “equipment” (ekipman). “equipped” ve “equipping” fiil biçimleri, “equips” çekimli fiildir; isim yerine geçemez.

s:
Read the paragraph and complete the missing word.

Glass frogs, found in the rainforests of Central and South America, are known for their see-through skin. When they sleep, they hide most of their red blood cells in the liver, which makes their bodies even more transpa___. Scientists believe this trick helps them avoid predators.

Which word correctly completes the unfinished word in the paragraph?
a: “make + nesne + sıfat” yapısında “more” ile birlikte sıfat gerekir: “even more transparent”. “transparency” ve “transparence” isim, “transparently” zarftır; nesneyi niteleyemez.

s:
Read the paragraph and complete the missing word.

Deserts are among the hottest places on Earth during the day. To avoid the heat, many desert animals rest in cool underground burrows unt___ the sun goes down. They then come out to search for food in the cooler night air.

Which word correctly completes the unfinished word in the paragraph?
a: Ardından gelen “the sun goes down” yan cümlesini bağlayan zaman bağlacı “until” (-e kadar) gerekir. “untie” fiil, “untrue” ve “untold” sıfattır; cümleyi bağlayamaz.

s:
Read the paragraph and complete the missing word.

Amateur astronomers have made real contributions to science. Using small telescopes in their backyards, they have spotted new comets and exploding stars. Their observ___ are often sent to professional observatories, which use them to confirm new discoveries.

Which word correctly completes the unfinished word in the paragraph?
a: Yüklem “are” çoğul olduğundan ve sonra “them” ile gönderme yapıldığından çoğul isim “observations” gerekir. Tekil “observation” uyuşmaz; “observed” ve “observing” “Their” sonrasında isim yerine geçmez.

s:
Read the paragraph and complete the missing word.

The new pedestrian bridge was designed to be both light and strong. Engineers chose a steel frame because it is flex___ enough to bend slightly in high winds without breaking. Older bridges in the city use heavier stone supports.

Which word correctly completes the unfinished word in the paragraph?
a: “be + sıfat + enough” yapısında sıfat gerekir: “flexible enough”. “flexibility” isim, “flexibly” zarftır; “is flexing enough” ise anlam olarak bükülme eylemini anlatır ve “to bend” ile çelişir.

s:
Read the paragraph and complete the missing word.

Before the printing press came into use in Europe in the fifteenth century, books there were copied by hand. A single copy of a long book could take months to produce. As a result, books rema___ rare and expensive for centuries.

Which word correctly completes the unfinished word in the paragraph?
a: Paragraf geçmişi anlatır ve özne “books” çoğuldur; geçmiş zaman “remained” gerekir. “remains” tekil özne ister, “remaining” tek başına yüklem olamaz, “remainder” isimdir.

s:
Read the paragraph and complete the missing word.

Early studies suggested that drinking coffee was harmful to the heart. However, many of these studies did not account for smoking, which was common among heavy coffee drinkers. When later researchers adju___ for smoking, the apparent link became much weaker.

Which word correctly completes the unfinished word in the paragraph?
a: Geçmiş anlatımda (“became”) çoğul özne “researchers” ile geçmiş zaman “adjusted” gerekir; “adjust for” bir değişkenin etkisini hesaba katmaktır. “adjusts” tekil ve şimdiki zaman, “adjustable” sıfat, “adjustment” isimdir.

s:
Read the paragraph and complete the missing word.

In many unrelated languages, the word for “mother” begins with a sound like “m.” Some linguists argue that this is not a coinc___ but a result of how babies first learn to speak: closing the lips is one of the easiest movements to make, and it naturally produces an “m” sound.

Which word correctly completes the unfinished word in the paragraph?
a: “not a … but a result” kalıbında “a” ile kullanılan sayılabilir isim gerekir: “coincidence” (tesadüf). “coincide” fiil, “coincidental” sıfat, “coinciding” fiil biçimidir; “a” sonrasında tek başına isim görevi görmez.

s:
Read the paragraph and complete the missing word.

Ice usually covers the lake from December to March. Last year, however, the winter was relati___ mild, and the ice never became thick enough for skating. Local businesses that rent skates reported their lowest income in decades.

Which word correctly completes the unfinished word in the paragraph?
a: Sıfatı (“mild”) niteleyen sözcük zarf olmalıdır: “relatively mild” (görece ılık). “relative” sıfat, “relation” ve “relativity” isimdir; başka bir sıfatın önünde derece bildiremez.

s:
Read the paragraph and complete the missing word.

Some seabirds, such as frigatebirds, can sleep while flying over the ocean. Rather than shutting down the whole brain, they often rest one half of it at a time, while the other half stays alert. This allows them to keep watch for danger wit___ landing.

Which word correctly completes the unfinished word in the paragraph?
a: Ardından -ing biçimi (“landing”) gelen ve “-meden” anlamı veren edat “without” olur. “within” yer/süre bildirir ve “landing” ile anlam kurmaz; “withdraw” ve “withhold” fiildir.

s:
Read the paragraph and complete the missing word.

Many museums now let visitors explore their collections online. Instead of trav___ long distances, students can examine high-resolution images of famous paintings from home. Some museums also offer live video tours led by curators.

Which word correctly completes the unfinished word in the paragraph?
a: “Instead of” bir edattır ve ardından fiil gelecekse -ing biçimi kullanılır: “Instead of traveling”. “travels” ve “traveled” çekimli fiil, “travelers” isimdir ve “long distances” nesnesini alamaz.

s:
Read the paragraph and complete the missing word.

Bilingual children sometimes mix two languages in a single sentence. Parents may worry that this shows confusion, but researchers have found that such mixing is usually system___: children tend to switch languages at points where the grammar of both languages allows it.

Which word correctly completes the unfinished word in the paragraph?
a: “is usually …” yapısında yüklem sıfatı gerekir: “systematic” (kurallı, düzenli). İki nokta sonrası açıklama da karışımın kurala bağlı olduğunu gösterir. “system/systems” isim, “systematize” fiildir.

s:
Read the paragraph and complete the missing word.

Large volcanic eruptions can affect weather far from where they occur. They send tiny particles high into the atmosphere, where the particles reflect part of the incoming sunlight back into space. The result can be a temporary drop in average global temper___ lasting a year or more.

Which word correctly completes the unfinished word in the paragraph?
a: Güneş ışığının geri yansıması ortalama küresel “temperature” (sıcaklık) değerini düşürür. “temperate” sıfattır (ılıman); “temperament” (mizaç) ve “temperance” (ölçülülük) isimdir ama bağlama uymaz.

s:
Read the paragraph and complete the missing word.

Critics of the policy argued that it would discourage investment. The data, however, offer little support for this claim: in the three years after the policy was introduced, investment in the region rose rather than fell. The critics’ prediction was, in effect, contra___ by the evidence.

Which word correctly completes the unfinished word in the paragraph?
a: Yatırım düşmek yerine arttığı için tahmin kanıtla “contradicted” (yalanlandı) olur; edilgen yapı geçmiş ortaç ister. “contrasted” “with” ile kullanılır, “contracted” (daraldı/sözleşme yaptı) anlamsızdır, “was contradicting by” dilbilgisi hatasıdır.

s:
Read the paragraph and complete the missing word.

Although the two frog species look almost identical, they rarely interbreed. Their mating calls differ in pitch, and females respond only to the calls of their own species. This behavioral barrier keeps the two populations genetically distin___ even where their ranges overlap.

Which word correctly completes the unfinished word in the paragraph?
a: “keep + nesne + sıfat” yapısında sıfat gerekir; “genetically” zarfı bu sıfatı niteler: “genetically distinct” (genetik olarak ayrı). “distinctly” zarf olduğu için nesneyi niteleyemez; “distinction” isim, “distinguished” (seçkin) anlama uymaz.

s:
Read the paragraph and complete the missing word.

The committee’s report was not intended to settle the debate. Its authors described their conclusions as provis___, noting that new data could easily change them. They recommended a second review once more evidence became available.

Which word correctly completes the unfinished word in the paragraph?
a: “describe X as + sıfat” yapısında sıfat gerekir: “provisional” (geçici, kesinleşmemiş); yeni verinin sonucu değiştirebileceği bilgisi de bunu doğrular. “provision” isim, “provisionally” zarf, “provisioned” (erzak sağlanmış) anlama uymaz.

s:
Read the paragraph and complete the missing word.

In the early twentieth century, the astronomer A. E. Douglass began measuring tree rings in the American Southwest. He hoped that the rings, which record a tree’s growth year by year, might reveal past changes in sunspot activity. That hope was never fully realized, but his work produced something more lasting: a method for dating wood with remarkable precision.

The method, known as dendrochronology, depends on the fact that ring width varies with growing conditions. In a dry year, a tree adds only a thin ring; in a wet year, a wider one. Because trees across a region experience the same weather, they share a distinctive sequence of thick and thin rings. By matching overlapping sequences from living trees, old buildings and buried logs, researchers can extend a chronology far back in time. A beam from an ancient dwelling can then be dated by finding where its pattern fits.

The technique has limits. It works poorly in many tropical regions, where trees may grow year-round and often do not form clear annual rings. Nevertheless, where it applies, it has become a standard check on other dating methods, including radiocarbon dating.

What is the passage mainly about?
c: How a method for dating wood developed and how it works
Why changes in sunspot activity affect the growth of trees
How tropical trees record the weather in their rings
Why radiocarbon dating has replaced tree-ring dating
a: Metin Douglass’ın çalışmasından doğan ağaç halkasıyla tarihleme yöntemini, işleyişini ve sınırlarını anlatır. Güneş lekesi beklentisi gerçekleşmemiştir; yöntem radyokarbonun yerini almamış, onu denetlemek için kullanılır.

Many plants depend on animals to move their seeds, and the best-known partners are birds and mammals that eat fruit. A less obvious partner is the ant. Thousands of plant species, from violets to certain acacias, produce seeds with a small attached structure called an elaiosome. Rich in fats and proteins, the elaiosome serves as a reward. Worker ants carry the seed back to the nest, where the elaiosome is removed and fed to the larvae. The seed itself, which is hard and largely unharmed, is then discarded, often in an underground chamber or on a waste pile near the nest.

For the plant, this arrangement offers several possible benefits. The seed is moved away from the parent plant, reducing competition between parent and offspring. Waste piles tend to be richer in nutrients than the surrounding soil, which may help seedlings establish themselves. Seeds that end up below ground may also be hidden from seed-eating rodents and, in fire-prone habitats, protected from flames.

The distances involved are modest, usually no more than a few meters. The value of ant dispersal, therefore, seems to lie less in how far seeds travel than in where they end up.

The word “modest” in the passage is closest in meaning to
a: “The distances involved are modest, usually no more than a few meters” cümlesinde “modest” mesafenin küçük olduğunu anlatır. “humble” ve “polite” sözcüğün kişiler için kullanılan “alçakgönüllü” anlamına dayanır.

Many plants depend on animals to move their seeds, and the best-known partners are birds and mammals that eat fruit. A less obvious partner is the ant. Thousands of plant species, from violets to certain acacias, produce seeds with a small attached structure called an elaiosome. Rich in fats and proteins, the elaiosome serves as a reward. Worker ants carry the seed back to the nest, where the elaiosome is removed and fed to the larvae. The seed itself, which is hard and largely unharmed, is then discarded, often in an underground chamber or on a waste pile near the nest.

For the plant, this arrangement offers several possible benefits. The seed is moved away from the parent plant, reducing competition between parent and offspring. Waste piles tend to be richer in nutrients than the surrounding soil, which may help seedlings establish themselves. Seeds that end up below ground may also be hidden from seed-eating rodents and, in fire-prone habitats, protected from flames.

The distances involved are modest, usually no more than a few meters. The value of ant dispersal, therefore, seems to lie less in how far seeds travel than in where they end up.

c: To contrast familiar seed carriers with a less obvious one
To show that ants compete with them for the same fruit
To explain why most plant seeds carry an elaiosome
To argue that they carry seeds shorter distances than ants
a: Yazar meyve yiyen kuş ve memelileri “best-known partners” olarak anar, ardından “A less obvious partner is the ant” der; amaç bilinen taşıyıcılarla daha az bilinen karıncayı karşılaştırmaktır.

s:
When people who share no common language need to communicate regularly, for example through trade, they often develop a simplified form of speech known as a pidgin. A pidgin typically draws most of its vocabulary from one language, usually that of the more powerful group, but has a reduced grammar: word endings may disappear, and ideas such as time are expressed with separate words rather than with changes to the verb. Crucially, a pidgin has no native speakers; everyone who uses it learned another language first.

This changes when children grow up in a community where a pidgin is widely used. Acquiring it as their first language, they expand it into a fully developed language, called a creole, with a stable grammar and the capacity to express any idea. Some creoles, such as Haitian Creole, are now the main language of millions of people.

Because creoles often take much of their vocabulary from European languages, they have sometimes been dismissed as “broken” versions of those languages. Linguists reject this view. A creole has its own consistent rules, and those rules frequently differ from the rules of the language that supplied its vocabulary.

According to the passage, what is one key difference between a pidgin and a creole?
c: A pidgin has no native speakers, but a creole does.
A pidgin borrows its words, but a creole invents them.
A pidgin is spoken by children, but a creole is not.
A pidgin has complex grammar, but a creole does not.
a: Metne göre pidginin anadili konuşucusu yoktur; çocuklar onu ilk dil olarak edindiğinde kreol oluşur, yani kreolün anadili konuşucuları vardır. Kreol de sözcüklerini çoğunlukla başka bir dilden alır.

s:
The Vasa: a warship that keeps teaching

A. On 10 August 1628, crowds gathered along the waterfront in Stockholm to watch the warship Vasa set out on her maiden voyage. She was among the most heavily armed ships of her day, carrying 64 guns on two gun decks, and her hull was decorated with hundreds of carved and painted sculptures intended to display the power of the Swedish crown. Yet after sailing only about a kilometre, the ship heeled over in a gust of wind, water poured in through the open gunports, and she sank in full view of the spectators. Of the people on board, a number lost their lives within sight of the shore.

B. An inquiry was held almost immediately, but it did not find anyone guilty. The ship’s dimensions had been approved by the king himself, and the master shipbuilder in charge of the project had died the year before she sailed, leaving others to complete his work. Modern analysis suggests that the fundamental problem was that the hull was too narrow and too high for the weight of guns and superstructure it carried, so the ship could not hold enough ballast low down to keep it upright. A stability test conducted before departure, in which thirty men ran from side to side across the deck, had in fact shown the ship rocking dangerously, but the test was stopped and the voyage went ahead.

C. For more than three centuries the wreck lay in about 32 metres of water in the harbour. Several factors explain why so much of it survived. The water in this part of the Baltic Sea is brackish, containing far less salt than the open ocean, and this makes it inhospitable to the shipworm, a wood-boring mollusc that destroys wooden wrecks in saltier seas. The cold, oxygen-poor conditions near the harbour floor also slowed the activity of other organisms. When the ship was finally raised in 1961, following a search led by the amateur researcher Anders Franzén, who had located the wreck in 1956, her hull was almost entirely intact.

D. Raising the ship, however, created a new problem. Waterlogged wood that is allowed to dry quickly shrinks and cracks, and a hull of this size could have been seriously damaged as its timbers lost their water. Conservators therefore sprayed the wood with polyethylene glycol, a water-soluble, wax-like substance that gradually takes the place of water inside the wood cells and supports them as the wood dries. The spraying continued for 17 years, from 1962 to 1979, and was followed by roughly nine years of slow drying. Only then could the ship be displayed in conditions resembling those of an ordinary museum.

E. Even this lengthy treatment did not end the story. Around the year 2000, staff noticed whitish and yellowish deposits forming on the surface of the timbers, and analysis showed that they were linked to the formation of acid. While the ship lay on the seabed, bacteria in the oxygen-poor water had produced sulphur compounds that soaked into the wood. Once the hull was exposed to air, these compounds began to react with oxygen, helped by iron from the ship’s corroded bolts, producing sulphuric acid. Over time, such acid can weaken wood from within, and similar problems have since been reported in other wrecks recovered from the sea.

F. Today the museum controls temperature and humidity carefully to slow these reactions, and researchers continue to monitor the hull for signs of movement and decay. In this sense, the Vasa has become a laboratory as well as an exhibit. Each solution has revealed a further problem, and the lessons learned in Stockholm are now applied to waterlogged wooden objects elsewhere. The ship that failed so spectacularly in 1628 has, in the end, proved remarkably useful.

c: An investigation that left no one to blame
A crowd that witnessed a famous disaster
A sea that protected a wreck for centuries
A treatment that took decades to complete
a: B paragrafı batışın ardından yapılan soruşturmanın kimseyi suçlu bulmadığını ve olası tasarım kusurlarını anlatır. Kalabalık A, Baltık suyunun koruması C, uzun süren koruma işlemi D paragrafının konusudur.

Of the people on board, a number lost their lives within sight of the shore.

B. An inquiry was held almost immediately, but it did not find anyone guilty. The ship’s dimensions had been approved by the king himself, and the master shipbuilder in charge of the project had died the year before she sailed, leaving others to complete his work. Modern analysis suggests that the fundamental problem was that the hull was too narrow and too high for the weight of guns and superstructure it carried, so the ship could not hold enough ballast low down to keep it upright. A stability test conducted before departure, in which thirty men ran from side to side across the deck, had in fact shown the ship rocking dangerously, but the test was stopped and the voyage went ahead.

The water in this part of the Baltic Sea is brackish, containing far less salt than the open ocean, and this makes it inhospitable to the shipworm, a wood-boring mollusc that destroys wooden wrecks in saltier seas. The cold, oxygen-poor conditions near the harbour floor also slowed the activity of other organisms. When the ship was finally raised in 1961, following a search led by the amateur researcher Anders Franzén, who had located the wreck in 1956, her hull was almost entirely intact.

s:
The desert locust: from loner to plague

A. For most of their lives, desert locusts are unremarkable insects. In their solitary form they are brownish in colour, avoid one another, and remain within relatively small areas of the arid and semi-arid lands that stretch from West Africa to South-West Asia. Yet under certain conditions the same species undergoes a striking transformation and becomes what the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) describes as the most destructive migratory pest in the world. This change is not a matter of genetic difference: an individual locust can switch between forms depending on its surroundings, a process known as phase change. Scientists have long been fascinated by this ability, since few other insects alter both their behaviour and their bodies so dramatically in response to the presence of their neighbours.

B. The trigger is crowding. After unusually heavy rains, vegetation flourishes in normally barren areas, and locusts breed rapidly. When the rains end and plants begin to die back, large numbers of insects are forced together into the shrinking patches of green that remain. Laboratory studies have shown that repeated contact between individuals, particularly touching of the hind legs, prompts a sharp rise in the chemical serotonin in the insects’ nervous systems, and within hours the locusts begin to seek one another out rather than keep apart. The gregarious form also changes in appearance: immature adults turn pink, while mature adults become yellow.

C. Once gregarious, locusts form bands of wingless young on the ground and, later, swarms of flying adults. According to the FAO, one square kilometre of swarm can contain between 40 and 80 million adults. Each adult eats roughly its own weight in fresh food every day, about two grams, so a single square kilometre of swarm can consume as much food in a day as about 35,000 people. Swarms generally fly with the wind and may cover anything from a few kilometres to more than 100 kilometres in a single day.

D. The impact of a plague falls most heavily on farming and herding communities that depend on a single harvest or on seasonal pasture. During quiet periods, known as recessions, desert locusts are usually confined to about 30 countries; during plagues, they may spread to parts of roughly 60 countries. Because a swarm can strip crops and grazing land within hours, the effects on food supplies and incomes can last long after the insects have moved on. In the past, some plagues have continued for several years before finally coming to an end, usually when a combination of control efforts and unfavourable weather reduced breeding.

E. Control today depends heavily on early warning. National teams survey breeding areas and send their findings to an FAO information service, which combines them with weather data, satellite images of vegetation and other habitat information in order to issue forecasts up to six weeks ahead. When infestations are found, the main method of control is still the spraying of small, concentrated doses of chemical pesticides from vehicles and aircraft. Biological alternatives, including products based on fungi that infect locusts, are being developed and used, but because they act more slowly, they are not yet suitable for every situation.

F. Experts emphasise that the most effective strategy is preventive. If small outbreaks are detected and treated before they merge into swarms, a full-scale plague may never develop, and far less pesticide is needed than when vast areas must be sprayed. The difficulty is that breeding areas are huge and often remote, and during long periods of calm, funding for monitoring tends to decline, at exactly the moment when continued watching matters most. For this reason, many specialists argue that steady, long-term investment in surveillance is cheaper than the emergency campaigns that follow a failure to act.

c: What makes the insects change their behaviour
How far a swarm is able to travel in one day
Why farming communities suffer most in plagues
How forecasts of new outbreaks are produced
a: B paragrafı kalabalıklaşmanın, özellikle arka bacaklara dokunmanın serotonini artırarak çekirgelerin birbirini aramaya başlamasına yol açtığını anlatır. Mesafe C, çiftçiler D, tahminler E paragrafındadır.
